notes:
The whole walkthrough is inside one wikitable cell alongside a map gallery, so the bullets arrive as one run-on line; read out, it is three top-level bullets and three sub-bullets, and the gallery is not a step.

Nothing in the page says you talk to Esha'ntarl to begin -- bullet 1 says you WALK INTO the palace and the cutscene fires. The palace is not a named entity, so the marker is put on Esha'ntarl, who is both the header's giver and the NPC named in the closing cutscene, and who stands in the same zone. That is a proximity trigger dressed as an NPC step and is flagged as such.

The three Promyvions are a genuine unordered set -- the page numbers nothing and the three slivers are independent -- so they share a group and all three draw at once. Each carries its OWN sliver as evidence, which is legal because they are three different key items; a strict ladder would have marked Holla alone until you happened to go there.

The three slivers are also printed in the header's Reward box, which normally bars them from being evidence. Here the walkthrough states outright that you take them from the Memory Fluxes on the 4th floor and only THEN return, so they are obtained at those steps and prove those steps, not the quest's end. Flagged evidence_is_reward so the demotion is taken and a human can check it.

The page writes 'Memory Fluxes'; the singular is what a live entity is called, so the singular is recorded. The two header Item Reqs (Whisper of the Wyrmking, carried in from Zilart Mission 17 / Storms of Fate, and the Note written by Esha'ntarl granted at step 1) are never mentioned again by the walkthrough, so neither is put on a step as a held requirement.

notes:
A five-rung ladder with nothing observable on it: the reward is a Familiarity cap raise and a fellow skill, no item and no key item changes hands anywhere, so every evidence field is a deliberate null.

Bullets 3, 4 and 5 are fight tactics for the Adventuring Fellow -- set it to Stalwart Shield, turn away when it calls 'Here it comes!', let it hold hate -- and the sub-bullets under 4 are alternatives to that advice. None of them is a step; a verb scan would have made three out of them. The unnumbered paragraph after bullet 2 describes Vassago and belongs to the fight, and the unnumbered line after bullet 5 is the outcome of it.

Step 2 is deliberately placed in Fei'Yin rather than in Qu'Bia Arena: a zone-typed target carries no marker at all, so the only useful position the step can hold is the arena entrance at Fei'Yin (K-8), which is the place the player actually has to find.

Neptune's Spire is NOT a zone -- the resolver has no id for it -- so the final door step is placed in Upper Jeuno, which is where the building stands and where the page's own category puts the quest. 'Door: Neptune's Spire' resolves as a real targetable entity, so that last rung keeps a marker.

'Quest Reqs: Familiarity Level of 85' is a Fellowship counter no packet reports, so it gates nothing here.

notes:
A clean four-rung escort. Bullet 5 ('you will have 30 minutes') is a timer, not a step, and no packet reports it -- it lives in step 3's note. Bullet 4 is not a step either on its own: it only says Wanzo-Unzozo spawns after the zone-in cutscene, and its three sub-bullets are handling advice. The one action in that whole stretch is bullet 6's 'quickly talk to him' when he stops, so bullets 4-6 merge into a single talk on him.

The Completion certificate is a header Item Req, not a Reward, so it is clean evidence and it is the only observable thing in the quest. The page is explicit that failing to talk before he vanishes loses it and the quest has to be redone, which is exactly the state the ladder will show: no certificate, still on step 3.

Bullets 2 and 3 are one journey -- 'head to Garlaige Citadel' and 'as soon as you zone in you will receive a cutscene' -- so they are one travel rung.

notes:
Bullet 4 is the interesting decision here. It is marked '(Optional)' and lists roughly thirty guard and bystander NPCs across Port and Northern San d'Oria who have flavour comments about the thief, with a second sub-list of the seven that actually give hints. None of them is required, none is observable, and none changes the quest: turning them into thirty optional rungs would bury the five real ones under a wall of markers. They are recorded here and nowhere else. The hint-givers, for the record, are Crilde, Rielle and Avandale in Port San d'Oria and Pepigort, Maurinne, Gilipese and Rodaillece in Northern San d'Oria.

The sub-bullet under bullet 3 -- '(Optional) you can attempt to trade the button to Altiret' -- is extra text on the way past, not a rung.

Bullets 5 and 6 are one step, not two: finding Esca in the tower and trading her the button are consecutive interactions with the same NPC in the same place, and splitting them would put an unmarkable rung between two markers on her. The trade is what produces the Gilt Glasses, so the merged step carries them as evidence.

Altiret's position is never given on the page; only Miene's (I-8) and Esca's (F-6) are. His steps therefore keep their zone and lose their grid rather than inventing one.

notes:
Six bullets, six steps, and unusually for this corpus every one of them is a real action -- there is nothing here to throw away.

The one loss is at step 1: 'Magian Mooglehood missive' comes back from the resolver as a key item whose NAME is not unique, so it has no id and stage C will drop the entry. It is recorded anyway rather than nulled, so the failure lands in quarantine where it is visible and an override can fix it, instead of disappearing into a null that reads as 'there was nothing here'. Step 2's Tandem Necklace +1 picks the ladder up immediately afterwards, so nothing is actually stranded.

Bullet 2 calls the (H-5) moogle 'the Magian Moogle' and bullet 3 calls the same one at the same coordinates 'Magian Moogle (Blue)'. Both fold to the same key, the colour is a wiki disambiguation rather than an in-game name, so the plain form is used and the zone is given on every rung -- an unzoned moogle is the one shape the validator forbids outright.

Step 4 is the trial itself. It has no zone, because the page gives none: Misareaux Coast Seaboard Vultures and Meriphataud Mountains (S) Condors are its SUGGESTIONS for a level-75-capped fellow, not the requirement, which is any 25 Bird-type creatures that give the fellow experience. Recording either as a mob would have turned advice into a rule, so mobs is empty. The necklace must be WORN, not merely held, which items cannot express, and the kill count is not observable, so the step has no evidence at all.

Steps 3 and 5 are the same trade to the same moogle with step 4 between them. That is not a wedge -- the page really does make you register the trial, go and kill, and come back to the same moogle.

'Job level 75+' is the level gate restated for any job, so jobs stays empty. 'Adventuring Fellow level 71+' and the header's [KI] Magian trial log are both real preconditions with no slot in the schema.

notes:
Bullets 2 and 3 are both routing to one place -- the entrance from Yhoator Jungle (G-6), the left fork, the black pillar at (I-9) on map 2, and the Unity 125 alternative -- so they fold into the trade rung rather than becoming an unmarkable travel rung of their own. The whole route is kept in that step's note; Ifrit's Cauldron is not a place to be vague about.

The obtain rung comes from bullet 1's sub-bullets, and it earns its place: Wild Pamamas is what the quest is actually about, it drops from Young Opo-opo in Yuhtunga Jungle or turns up on the Auction House, and holding it is the one observable thing in the quest. Without that rung the ladder would sit on Hari Pakhroib until the very last trade.

The header's OR is real but lopsided: first completion needs Wild Pamamas, subsequent completions take Wild Pamamas -or- Wild Melon. So the melon is recorded as items_alt on the trade, where 'either one satisfies' is exactly right, but NOT as evidence on the obtain rung, because on a first run holding a melon proves nothing.

Two sub-bullets are corrections rather than instructions and stay as notes: the NPC asks for Ice Clusters you do not need on this route, and asks you to shout your name at the altar, which the page says is unnecessary.

VERIFY: step 2 downgraded to medium. The page makes that rung soft in two directions and neither is expressible: Wild Pamamas 'can also sometimes be found on the Auction House', so the recorded Yuhtunga Jungle zone need never be visited, and Item Reqs allows a Wild Melon instead on subsequent completions, so a repeat player on the melon path never holds the evidence and the mark strands on step 2 instead of advancing to the Altar. The evidence is kept because it is correct on a first completion, which is the path the walkthrough actually describes.

notes:
The header's giver is Romualdo in Batallia Downs (S), but the walkthrough is explicit that the FIRST thing you do is speak to a different Romualdo, the present-day one at Metalworks (K-9), and that the quest does not even appear in your log until the step after that. A player sent straight to the past gets nothing. Start is therefore moved to Metalworks and the header's string kept verbatim in start.raw; both Romualdos are real, so this is a marker moved between two working positions, not a marker rescued from a broken one.

Nothing observable happens anywhere in this quest -- the reward is a Smart Grenade handed over at the end and no key item is involved -- so every evidence field is null on purpose.

Bullets 7 and 8 sit under 'Some post-quest cutscenes are available that award the proper title' and their bullet numbers continue the same list. They are after the quest is already complete, so they are optional rather than dropped: the title is the only thing at stake and the page names the dialogue option ('Message on the Wind') you have to pick. They are left ordered rather than grouped because the page presents Romualdo first and Childerich second.

Four '(Optional) speak again for additional text' sub-bullets are extra dialogue and are not rungs.

Childerich's position is given once, at (E-12) by the Old Cabin in Grauberg (S). Bullets 5 and 8 do not restate it; (E-12) is carried forward and those two steps are marked medium for it -- bullet 8 in particular is post-quest and the page never says whether he is still there. Fame 'Crystal War' is not one of the addon's nine regions, so it gates nothing and only raw is kept.

VERIFY: step 7 downgraded to medium for consistency with steps 5 and 8. Bullet 7 says only 'Speak to Romualdo in present' -- it restates neither Metalworks nor (K-9), both of which are carried forward from bullet 1, and like step 8 it is post-quest, so the page never confirms he is still standing there. The draft applied that reasoning to steps 5 and 8 but not to step 7.

notes:
Two numbered bullets, but four things actually happen, and the page buries two of them in sub-bullets.

The Rhinostery certificate is printed in the header's Reward box, which normally bars it from being evidence. Read the page though: bullet 1 hands it to you at the START, and its own sub-bullet says it is what gets you into Toraimarai Canal. It is a mid-quest access key that the wiki also lists as a keepsake. Used as step 1's evidence and flagged, which costs the quest a confidence tier and is worth it -- it is the only thing that can move the mark off Ohbiru-Dohbiru. On a repeat run you already hold it and the ladder opens on the canal, which is exactly right.

Speaking to Seven of Diamonds at Windurst Walls (H-3) is a rung, not routing: it is a named NPC at a given grid and it is the only way in. The rest of that sub-bullet tree -- east at the first intersection, down at (I-8), right twice at (I-10), up at (I-9), west to (G-9) -- is a route through one zone and stays in the note.

The unnumbered closing line is bullet 2 restated, not a fifth thing to do.

The preamble ('if you had just completed the previous quest, you must zone first') is a precondition on step 1.

notes:
Three named clickable objects carry this quest -- Occultist Footprints, the Hostage Tent and the Seat of Gramk-Droog -- and all three resolve, so five of the six rungs are markable even though nothing in the quest is observable. The reward is EXP and Bayld, so every evidence field is null on purpose.

Bullets 3 and 4 are one rung. 'Check the Hostage Tent' then 'buff up and check it again' are consecutive interactions with the same object in the same spot; the spawn is recorded on that rung. Bullet 5 is genuinely two things, though -- kill the Sentinel AND check the tent a third time -- so it splits, and the fight sits between two tent rungs because the page really does put it there.

The four sub-bullets under bullet 3 are a route, not steps: Bivouac #2, southeast over the river, the tunnel by the small watch tower at (J-9/10), the vine by the tent/reive with the small cave in the southeast corner of (I-10), then northwest through the tunnel under the waterfall. Marjami Ravine is not a place to leave a player guessing, so it is kept whole in the note.

Bullet 2 gives a border, '(I-6) / (J-6)', not a point; (I-6) is recorded and the border is noted. Fame 'Seekers of Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.

check it once for a short cutscene, then buff up and check it AGAIN to spawn the Velkk Sentinel. Route: warp to Bivouac #2, head southeast over the river, enter the tunnel by the small watch tower at (J-9/10), climb the vine at the tent/reive (small cave to the left, southeast corner of I-10), then northwest through the tunnel that runs under the waterfall.
